reasons.specificity: The reading closely tracks Castoriadis’s distinct boundaries of regime-defined costs, monetary valuation, firm-level imputation, fuzzy collective production, and global heterogeneity.
reasons.anchoring: F1–F12 quote the supplied paper accurately and generally support the interpretations, with only minor overextension such as treating immanent critique as an alternative boundary.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes accounting omission from material harm, legal attribution from causal containment, and national closure from homogeneous planetary framing.
reasons.coherence: The main argument and tables are consistent, but the repeated claims of complete yet unchecked and inconclusive coverage, plus malformed-record diagnostics, create internal and evidentiary incoherence.
reasons.usefulness: The inclusion/exclusion/consequence inventory and clearly labeled analyst reframings are valuable with the text open, though the duplicated scope machinery substantially obstructs the reading.
reasons.hallucination_risk: The textual interpretation is well supported, but CHECK identifiers, recorded outcomes, validation errors, malformed scope records, and lost-anchor warnings are unsupported by anything supplied.

decisive_errors.analysis_claim: The scope sections report complete coverage, unchecked review status, malformed associated records, validation errors, and findings that lost anchor evidence.
decisive_errors.counter_passage: No passage in the supplied paper contains review metadata, CHECK records, Pydantic validation errors, coverage reports, or lost-anchor warnings; the source ends with notes and abbreviations.
decisive_errors.why_decisive: These are invented provenance and audit claims presented as reported facts, not analyst proposals or source claims.

score.one_line: An unusually strong and well-anchored boundary reading is materially weakened by extensive invented review-system metadata and an overclassification of immanent critique as a boundary alternative.
